chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, raising it from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), said:
He was asked about a man in the desert who was unable to give the Fitra. He said: 'He should give in charity four Artals of milk.'

key_terms.أَرْطَال: Artals, a traditional unit of weight or volume used for measuring goods
key_terms.الْبَادِيَة: The desert or countryside, referring to a rural or remote area
key_terms.الْفِطْرَة: Fitra, the obligatory alms-tax paid at the end of Ramadan or on specific occasions

ai.seo_question: What is the alternative payment for Fitra if one lives in the desert and cannot provide the usual food?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the Shia juristic principle of substituting the standard Fitra (typically wheat or barley) with locally available goods, specifically milk, for those in remote desert areas. It highlights the practical flexibility of the Imams in adapting religious obligations to environmental constraints, ensuring that the poor can still fulfill their duty without undue hardship. This ruling underscores the broader Islamic emphasis on ease and accessibility in worship, reflecting the dynamic nature of fiqh in addressing diverse geographical contexts.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, 
(It has been narrated) raising it from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘He<sup>asws</sup>
was asked about a man in the desert, who was unable to give the Fitra’. Heasws said: ‘He should give in charity with four Ratls (a unit of measurement) of milk’.
en.sarwar: 15. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from in a marfu‘ manner who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,
about a man who lives in a remote village and is not able to pay al-Fitrah. He (the Imam) said, ’He is required to pay by four Artal of milk.”’
